text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The parties of the ruling coalition are to sign the new cabinet declaration and government coalition treaty.
- According to a twice-yearly study by the Corporate Resources Group, a private consulting company, the cost of living in Riga is higher than in two other Baltic capitals, Vilnius and Tallinn.
- The cabinet of outgoing prime minister Andris Shkele held its last meeting to consider a record number of government documents.
- The commander of the Home Guard has ordered paramilitary organisations not to use weapons during road checks on roads, after one of their members killed a driver who failed to stop at a road check.
- Shkele's advisors told the newspaper that after leaving his post the ex-premier plans to set up a new company, which may employ some of his political team.
- Latvian air force commander Karlis Kins died in a car crash on the Riga-Liepaja highway, 50 km from the capital.

- Small creditors of the collapsed Bank Baltija, whose deposits were partly compensated by the government in 1995, are receiving letters from liquidator, David Berry, turning down claims to the rest of the money.
- The average salary in the public sector was 132.96 lats.
- Oleg S, arrested by the Estonian police on suspicion of being the internet blackmailer Viktor, sent a letter to the newspaper, saying he is not guilty.
- The new majority shareholder of Riga meat packing plant, Estonia's Rakvere, is expected to invest one million dollars to renovate the plant and for training.
- Latvian exporters prefer using maritime transport, 73 percent of total exports, while importers prefer the railways at 74 percent of total imports.
